f5d0810b-8d0e-4bee-b85c-e93f19ab3aef.description: BambooHR Privacy Policy Job Openings Software Engineer - Datapath Engineering - R D - San Jose, California (Hybrid) SOFTWARE ENGINEER - DATAPATH Turn a customer’s intent into a live, multi-cloud network — automatically, anywhere in the world — and learn the entire stack while you do it. THE MISSION When a company connects its data centers, clouds, and offices on Alkira , our team is what makes it happen. The customer tells us what they want — connect these networks, across these clouds, with these policies — and we turn that into a real, working network in minutes instead of weeks, automatically. We’re the Playbooks / Orchestration team, and we build that automation. Using a mix of Ansible, Python, and Go, we set up the networking stack on our Cloud Exchange Points (CXPs) and run the workflows that keep it healthy — including tricky operations like safely restarting a node. We bring up new virtual network functions (VNFs), build the tooling and CLI used to inspect and configure each node, and work closely with the Routing, Data Path, and Backend teams. Our team spans the US and India, and above all we make sure every customer network comes up correctly and reliably, across every cloud. LOCATION: This is a hybrid work environment that requires onsite at San Jose, CA HQ on Tuesdays and Thursdays WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON Automate the cloud. Write the Ansible playbooks that provision infrastructure and stand up network services across AWS, Azure, and GCP — VPCs/VNets, subnets, tunnels, NAT, routing, and security policy. Build the engines. Develop the Go task engines that push this configuration onto the CXP nodes at scale — running provisioning and teardown against live state, and rebuilding a node’s entire configuration after a controlled restart. Bring up new capabilities. Integrate new VNFs as we light up new services and capabilities. Own the tooling. Build the Python tooling and CLI engineers use to inspect, configure, and debug the networking stack on the nodes. Model the work. Extend the configuration and task models that translate a single provisioning request into the exact commands applied on the nodes. Keep it fast and correct. Help connectivity stay correct, fast, and reliable across clouds and at scale. Solve real problems. Chase tricky production provisioning issues to their root cause and drive the fix — and collaborate with Routing, Data Path, and Backend on how configuration flows end to end. You won’t touch all of this on day one. Most engineers start in one layer and grow outward fast. WHO YOU ARE We’re looking for a well-rounded Software Engineer with a basic grounding in networking technologies. Our stack spans several layers — Ansible playbooks, Go task engines, Python tooling, the networking stack on the nodes — and sits right next to the C-based data path. You don’t need to be an expert in all of it. Bring strong fundamentals and real curiosity about how networks and clouds work, and you’ll start in one layer and grow into the rest. You'll thrive here if you have: Strong software fundamentals — data structures, problem-solving, clean code, and the patience to debug. Hands-on coding in at least one of C, Python, or Go, and the appetite to pick up the others — we use all three everyday, and the engineers who range across them go furthest. Comfort on Linux — the shell, processes, logs, and the everyday networking tools. Hands-on familiarity with core networking — TCP/IP, and the curiosity to go deeper. A working mental model of the cloud — at least one of AWS, Azure, or GCP: what a VPC/VNet, subnet, and security group actually are. A debugging mindset — you genuinely enjoy chasing a problem until you find the real cause. Bonus Points Ansible or other configuration-automation experience. You use AI-assisted development tools like Claude Code — we lean on them to build workflows, write debug tooling, and move faster across the entire software development lifecycle. Experience building CLIs, task runners, or automation that runs at scale. Familiarity with firewalls, load balancers, and similar network services. WHY YOU’LL GROW FAST HERE The orchestration layer touches every part of the system — clouds, Linux, the networking stack, and the data path next door. That makes it one of the best vantage points in the company for an early-career engineer: you’ll get unusually broad exposure, work shoulder-to-shoulder with networking and systems experts, and build a deep, end-to-end picture of how a real cloud network works. Strong all-rounders here don’t stay in one lane — they move fluidly between layers and become the people who understand how the whole thing fits together. ON-CALL On-call is a mandatory part of this role. You’ll join the orchestration on-call rotation and help debug and resolve production provisioning issues, with coverage coordinated across the US and India. It’s also where a lot of the deepest learning happens — there’s no faster way to understand a system than to keep it running. ABOUT ALKIRA Alkira, a Lumen company , is building the future of enterprise networking: one programmable platform to connect, secure, and operate every cloud, site, partner, data center, and AI workload. Founded by Amir and Atif Khan, the creators of Viptela and pioneers of the SD-WAN market, Alkira was built to radically simplify how enterprises deploy and manage network infrastructure. Today, as part of Lumen, we are bringing that cloud-native operating model to a global network foundation trusted by the world’s largest enterprises. Our platform helps customers move faster without managing hardware, stitching together providers, or operating fragmented cloud networks. Teams can build and scale connectivity on demand, apply consistent security and segmentation, and gain visibility across distributed environments from one place. Meet the Team Join a team dedicated to performing failure analysis and debug of transceiver and optical engine multi-chip modules. Your Impact As a Failure Analysis Engineer, you will perform hands-on debug and failure analysis of transceiver products and optical engine components to identify root causes and drive corrective actions. Ability to collaborate effectively in a fast-paced environment while taking ownership of technical issues. Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with the application of coherent transceivers in optical networks. Strong failure analysis techniques at the subsystem, component, and device levels. manual:ed3d909c4d48.description: Uniswap Labs is a core contributor to the Uniswap Protocol, the world's largest DEX, with over $4 trillion in volume across 17 chains. Almost nobody in crypto hires and develops early-career engineers in a structured way — we're going to. You'll join one of our engineering pods, ship production code in your first weeks, and be paired with a dedicated senior engineer who owns your growth. We shape engineers full-stack from the start: you won't be boxed into one layer of the stack, and where you land long-term will follow your strengths. What you'll do Ship well-tested production code used by millions — across web, backend services, infrastructure, and (if it's your thing) smart contracts Work side-by-side with your assigned senior mentor and pod: pairing, code review, and real ownership rather than a training track Move across parts of the stack as you grow — we care that you learn to build complete products, not just components Work in person with the team at our NYC headquarters, 5 days a week What we look for A degree in Computer Science or a related field completed (or completing) between December 2024 and September 2026 Evidence that you build: internships, shipped side projects, open-source contributions, hackathon results — include links (GitHub, live apps, write-ups) Strong CS fundamentals and the ability to pick up new languages and systems quickly Genuine excitement about crypto and DeFi — no prior crypto experience required Able to work from our New York office 5 days per week Nice to have Anything you've built on or around crypto — a contract, a bot, a dashboard, a hackathon project Depth in whatever tools you build with — we don't screen for a specific language or framework, and we'd rather see one thing you've built deeply than a keyword list Competitive programming, CTFs, research, or open-source work Love for unicorns :) Minimum full-time salary of $138,400–$198,000.
